 Judgment
The Police Sub-Inspector of R.T.Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for
the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 324, 506 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 Smt.Mustaqueem was solemnized with accused in the year 2003 and from this marriage, two children were born.
Thereafter the accused started harassing CW1 and subjected her to both physical and mental cruelty for fetching dowry and hence started to live separately.
She filed divorce petition before the Court and also complained twice against accused with R. T. Nagara police station and the same are pending on the file of this court.

That being so, on 02-01-2023 KABC030575152020 CC No.7967/2023 at about 9.15 p.m. when CW1 walking on the 5 th Cross, Opp Vatican School, Dinnur Main, within the limits of R. T. Nagara Police Station for purchase of vegetables, at that time, the accused abused her in filthiest language and voluntarily beaten her with hands and stone and caused bleeding injury.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt.Mustaqueem, CW9- PSI of R. T. Nagara police Station registered a Crime No.02/2023 against the accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 504, 323, 324 of IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4.
Investigation:
The said police have registered FIR against accused person and recorded the statement of witnesses and secured wound certificate of CW1.
After completion of investigation, the IO/CW9 submitted charge sheet against accused for the above said offences.
5. The accused was released on bail by the order dated 11/09/2024.
6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offences alleged against the accused.
KABC030575152020 CC No.7967/2023 7. Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Senior APP and counsel for accused, the charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.323, 324, 504 of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried by giving the charge for offence punishable under section 498A of IPC as C. C. No.23267/2022 was filed for section 498A of IPC.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 9 witnesses however examined one witness and exhibited 2 documents.

The learned Sr.APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose R T Nagar Police Station vs Jabbevulla on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115569449/
2 would be served as the material witness has not supported the case by the order dated 11-09-2024.

sentences.text: 10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 02-01-2023 at about 9.15 p.m. when CW1 walking on the 5th Cross, Opp Vatican School, Dinnur Main, within the limits of R.
T. Nagara Police Station for purchase of vegetables, at that time, the accused abused her in filthiest language thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable U/sec. 504 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said date, place and time the accused has voluntarily beaten her with hands thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable U/sec. 323 of IPC?

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said date, place and time the accused has voluntarily beaten her with stone and caused bleeding injury thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable U/sec. 324 of IPC?
4.
What order?

13. The courts's findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 -3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 -3: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined witness, which is as follows KABC030575152020 CC No.7967/2023 i.
CW1 by name Smt.Mustaqueem - Informant examined as PW1 and deposed her that she has identified her signatures on Ex.P1 -complaint and Ex.P2-spot mahazar.
When she went to police station for setting right of minor differences amongst her and accused, the police obtained her signatures on these documents.
She pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex. P. 1 and Ex. P. 2.
She had not lodged any complaint against accused.
She obtained treatment from the hospital, as she fell down and caused injury.
She voluntarily admitted in her evidence that she has obtained divorce from accused.
No panchanama was drawn in her presence.

In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has R T Nagar Police Station vs Jabbevulla on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115569449/
3 cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness however no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

entities.text: R T Nagar Police Station vs Jabbevulla
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. PW1 is the informant cum victim has not supported the prosecution case.
Though the prosecution has cross examined her by treating as hostile witness, no favorable evidence from her to support the prosecution case and she has deposed falsely to help the accused.

In the present case,
the learned Sr. APP prays for issue of witness summons to other witnesses.

This court is of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined by the prosecution and if they supported the prosecution KABC030575152020 CC No.7967/2023 case that would not helpful as PW1 being informant cum victim did not support the prosecution case.
This court has dispensed with the evidence of other witnesses which could be only formal in nature.
Therefore, the prayer of learned Senior APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed.

16. It is a settled law that in order to bring home guilt of accused, the prosecution is required to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt but in the case on hand, absolutely there are no materials to connect the accused in the commission of the alleged offences as discussed above.
The prosecution miserably failed to prove that the accused is guilt of alleged offences beyond all reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answers point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.
17. Point No.4:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 3, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.323, 324, 504 of IPC.
KABC030575152020 CC No.7967/2023 (ii) Accused is set at liberty.
( iii )
In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six) months.
(iv) After the expiry of appeal period, the properties shown under PF No.02/2023 being worthless shall be destroyed.
(v) Ordered accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer, typed by steno, verified and corrected by me, then the judgment pronounced by me in the open court, on this the 13th day of September, 2024) (Deepa.V.), VIII Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
